name: Wish list
description: Calmer's package in Balance's skin: proof up front, questions in an ask, echo, teach, preview rhythm on every goal path, a named result profile and a progress graph, then today's paywall. Built as if templates were free.

title: Less stress. Better sleep.
Adapted to you.
cards.sub: Already have an account? Log in

notes.why: Proof on screen 1 kept to the 3 badges (Alex: coaches plus awards was too much). Version B for the team to react to: the coach faces with 'Developed by neuroscientists, meditation teachers and behavioral coaches' instead of the badges. Headline is the variant winning the live welcome-card test (b_benefit). The welcome card is payload-configurable, so this is config, not a release.
notes.evidence: Alex 1:40; ABCD test b_benefit; March A3; no clinical advisory claim exists, so the whitepaper's 'developed by experts in neuroscience, meditation instruction, and behavioral coaching' is the honest ceiling
fills: Badges are text-only on purpose (Apple rejected a laurel with its logo in 2022); confirm wording with marketing
Rating and count pulled Sep 4, 2026 (4.88, 120,363 US ratings); refresh before shipping

title: Let's start with a
few questions.
cards.body: Your answers shape your Plan: what your first session works on, how long it runs, and how it adapts from there. It takes about 3 minutes.

notes.why: Tell people what the questions do before asking them. Replaces the current 'Answer a few questions to personalize your experience' card.
notes.evidence: Alex 2:12; benchmark rule 2 (reason in the header)

notes.why: Name early is the cheapest enabler of the answer-echo register. The keyboard card validates first_name today, and text/textImage cards already replace a name placeholder.
notes.evidence: Benchmark: name is the field's 2nd most common ask (74%); rule 3 (result points back to what you said)

title: How old are you?
cards.subtitle: Your guidance will be tailored to your age group.
cards.reassure: Used only to tune your program. Never shown to anyone.

notes.why: Age bands instead of the numpad (the web funnel asks bands first). Existing subtitle kept as the reason line; reassurance added because the deck has none anywhere.
notes.evidence: Alex 2:34 (who-you-are first); benchmark rule 4; web funnel /age

title: How do you identify?
cards.subtitle: Optional. Some members prefer sessions that speak to their experience.

notes.why: Calmer opens on gender and echoes it later. Kept (Alex, Sep 4); the echo stays light because a round-2 tester read Calmer's gendered copy as 'given to every woman'.
Moved early (it sits next to the paywall today) and gains a one-line health-professional option so referrals become a proof signal. Reason line cut (Alex).
notes.evidence: Matheus: HDYHAU sits too close to the paywall; benchmark rule 2; Insight Timer offers 'Health Professional'
fills: Confirm the new answer_id with data (Balance HDYHAU buckets differ from Elevate's)

title: {{a.name}}, you're in
the right place.
cards.body: Balance has helped {{L.age_count}} people your age.{{H.pick(a.hdyhau==='family_and_friends',' Someone you know is one of them.','')}} Here's how it works: a 10-minute session each day, built from your answers and guided by 2 real coaches, plus a sleep library and Singles for the moments you need one.

rows.s: For the moment you need one

notes.why: Show the product before asking anything personal, and reflect back what the user just gave: their name, the age-specific member count (March's strongest confidence builder) and the friend referral when there was one. Newcomers in round 2 reached a paywall without knowing what the app would do for them.
fills: Session length and 'made from your answers' mechanism: confirm with Anna

notes.why: Kept exactly as today, per Alex. Hardcoded in Lua, not authorable.

title: How often do you
feel stressed?
cards.subtitle: Over the last 2 weeks. It sets the pace of your first week.

notes.why: Existing card with a 2-week window and a reason line.

title: How does stress usually
show up for you?
cards.subtitle: Select all that apply. Your sessions focus on what you pick.

notes.why: Same question, now multi-answer. The top quiz friction in March was being forced to pick one symptom. The question card already supports allowMultipleAnswers (unused in today's deck), so the icons and pastel rows stay.

title: Stress like this is why
most people start.
cards.body: You said stress shows up as {{H.lower(H.list(L.how_experience_stress))}}. That's the pattern members describe most. In a survey of 3,700+ members, 77% said they respond to stress better. Your first sessions are built for it.

notes.why: Validation beat that reads the answer back within seconds. Today the flow asks 8 to 10 questions and reflects none of them until the loading screen.

title: Meditation lowers
stress and anxiety.
cards.body: The most widely cited meta-analysis of meditation, 47 randomized trials and 3,500+ participants, found measurable improvements in anxiety, depression and pain.
cards.cite: Goyal et al., JAMA Internal Medicine, 2014. Results vary from person to person. Balance is not a substitute for professional care.

notes.why: Honest replacement for Calmer's agitation arc: one cited finding plus a disclaimer. The DID-YOU-KNOW-with-citation template (title, text, subtext) exists and is unused.
fills: Disclaimer wording with content

title: Singles, for the
moment stress hits.
cards.body: Singles are short sessions for right now: a rising panic, a hard conversation, a night you can't switch off. You'll find them on your Today screen from day 1.

notes.why: Section preview as felt value, and Calmer's 'look for the helicopter' trick: teach an affordance in onboarding that is visibly waiting on home.
notes.evidence: Alex 5:40 ('we literally have the same meditation, the SOS single')
fills: Real Single titles and durations from the catalog

title: Meet Ofosu and Leah,
your coaches.
cards.subtitle: They'll guide you toward {{H.goalsPhrase(a)}}.

bios.name: Ofosu
bios.text: Has taught meditation for over 20 years, including at the Insight Meditation Society and Spirit Rock.

bios.name: Leah
bios.text: Brings neuroscience, psychology and her own practice to every session. Has taught in 16+ countries.

cards.body: Every session is written and recorded by the 2 of them, then pieced together for you from your answers. Your first session is with Ofosu. Switch anytime.

Showcase, not chooser; no 'AI' in the copy.
notes.evidence: handcrafted-coaches-screen-angles.md; 3 competitors lean on teacher credibility

title: Your starting point.

stress.name: The Overdrive Mind
stress.insight: Your mind rarely gets to idle. {{H.exp(a)}} and {{H.days(a)}}, so week 1 is short sessions that teach your mind how to settle.

sleep.name: The Wired and Tired
sleep.insight: Your body is ready for rest before your mind is. {{H.exp(a)}}, so week 1 starts with the wind-down, then works on the stress underneath it.

mood.name: The Weather Watcher
mood.insight: Your mood moves with the day. {{H.exp(a)}} and {{H.days(a)}}, so week 1 is short check-ins that notice what you feel before it takes over.

focus.name: The Open Browser
focus.insight: Attention keeps opening new tabs. {{H.exp(a)}}, so week 1 trains it to come back in sessions short enough to finish.

cards.cite: Based only on your answers. Not a clinical assessment.

notes.template: goalMeditationPrimer (static per goal) or new gauge template
notes.why: A named result profile is where 'it understood me' landed in round 2. Sub-scores derive only from answers actually given, so no manufactured headroom (P18). The insight speaks back to experience and schedule.
notes.evidence: Round 2 A4; Alex 8:09; web funnel 'Here's Your Mental Health Profile / The Overdrive Mode'
fills: Profile names: content pass
Score mapping: agree the rules with DS so nothing reads as a diagnosis

title: Save your program.
cards.body: Create an account so your program follows you across devices and your trial reminder reaches you.
cards.sub: By creating your account, you agree to Balance's Terms and Privacy Policy.

notes.why: Wish list moves account creation after the trial starts. Sign-up before the paywall is a cross-device/CRM decision, so this is a Swift bookend change and a strategy call, not deck work.
notes.evidence: Growth Gems item 3; benchmark: deferred account gate is the norm for Balance's archetype

title: Prototype ends here.
cards.body: In the app, a started trial hands off to the first session on the Today screen. A decline shows today's counter-offer, then lands on the Today screen with the program locked.
cards.note: This is the wish-list version: the flow as we'd build it with no template limits. The constrained version keeps the same spine using only card templates that exist in the app today.

notes.why: End card for reviewers.
